FLASHCARD SET · AGES 4–5 YEARS

Sight Word flashcards.

Fifty-two cards for the small words that appear on every page of a first book: a, the, I, can, see, blue and the rest. Each card shows one word in big, clear letters over a friendly picture, ready to hold, read and spot in a story.

These cards belong to Class 29 · Storytime & Pre-Reading Comprehension on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Tap any card to open it.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Three new cards a day

    Pick three words, read each aloud together and let your child say it back. Add a new card only when the old ones feel easy, and stop while it is still fun.

  2. 02

    Hide and find

    Tape a few cards around a room and call out one word at a time. Your child hunts it down, reads it and carries it back.

  3. 03

    Spot it in a story

    Choose today’s word, then look for it together in a favourite picture book. A cheer for every one you find makes the word stick.

  4. 04

    Build a tiny sentence

    Lay two or three cards in a row, such as “I can run”, and read the line together. Swap one card for another and read it again.

      A Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The shortest word in the set is also one of the busiest, and it is the first card in the pile.

      How the card helps

      One raised finger links the word to the idea of one, so a child has a picture to hang it on.

      A quick game

      Spread five cards face up and ask your child to hand you the one that says a. Swap roles.

      What it teaches

      Your child learns to spot the shortest word on the page and the thing-words it keeps company with.

      Print it like this

      Print it and put it at the front of the shelf where the early readers live.

      One more idea

      Use the soft uh sound when reading a sentence, and the letter name only when singing the alphabet.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the lesson for “A” on the Learning Path.

      From the Sight Words (Class 29) class on the Learning Path.

      The Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The most-used word in English gets a card of its own, so it is worth meeting early.

      How the card helps

      The book with the word on its cover shows where the belongs: right in front of something you can name.

      A quick game

      Read a short rhyme aloud and tap the card each time you say the. Count the taps at the end.

      What it teaches

      Your child learns to hear a tiny word that hides in front of nearly every thing-word.

      Print it like this

      Print it at eye level on the bookshelf, where the busiest word belongs.

      One more idea

      Play hunt the the: read a line aloud and let your child stop you whenever they catch it.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the lesson for “The” on the Learning Path.

      From the Sight Words (Class 29) class on the Learning Path.

      I Flashcard for Preschoolers

      One letter, always capital, always standing tall: the word every child says about themselves.

      How the card helps

      Pointing at himself with both hands shows the word means the person speaking, which is easy for a child to act out.

      A quick game

      Take turns tapping your chest and finishing a sentence that begins with I.

      What it teaches

      Your child learns who a sentence is about when someone talks about themselves.

      Print it like this

      Print it and hang it at child height beside the mirror.

      One more idea

      Always read it inside a sentence at least once, so your child learns what the word does.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the lesson for “I” on the Learning Path.

      From the Sight Words (Class 29) class on the Learning Path.

      You Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The word that points at the listener: a small card with a big job in conversation.

      The finger aimed straight out of the card shows the word means whoever is looking, so your child is the you.

      A quick game

      Hold the card up to a teddy, to your child and to a family member, and say a sentence for each.

      What it teaches

      Your child learns to tell the speaker from the listener.

      Print it like this

      Print it and stick it on the fridge door, where everyone will see it.

      One more idea

      Pair it with the I card and read both: I see you.

      Me Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The word for the person on the receiving end, found in the sentences children say all day.

      Hands crossed over his chest on the card make me look like a hug, so the word feels warm.

      A quick game

      Hide the card, then peek it out from behind a book and say Look at me! Let your child do the same.

      What it teaches

      Your child learns that a person can be the one things happen to, not only the one doing them.

      Print it like this

      Print it and place it beside the mirror, next to the my card.

      One more idea

      My Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The word that says something belongs to you, and children use it with pride. Print it, tuck it in a bag and watch the pride show.

      A boy tapping his own chest proudly turns the word into a gesture of ownership your child can copy.

      A quick game

      Gather a few belongings on a rug and let your child claim each one aloud with my.

      What it teaches

      Your child learns that a small word can show who something belongs to.

      Print it like this

      Print it and tape it to your child's own door or cubby, where the word is true.

      One more idea

      Ask your child to point out a thing that is mine in the room, and then a thing that is yours.

      Are Flashcard for Preschoolers

      The word that goes with more than one person or thing. Once your child knows it, plural sentences in books start to make sense.

      How the card helps

      Two children pointing at themselves and at each other on the card show a pair, which is what are describes.

      A quick game

      Point at two toys and say Those are cars. Point at one and say That is a car.

      What it teaches

      Your child learns the difference between a word for one thing and a word for many.

      Print it like this

      Print it and put it next to a pair of items, such as two shoes.

      One more idea

      Sing a line from a favorite song and listen for are together.
